nom: La Roche-Posay Anthelios Ultra Light Fluid Face Sunscreen SPF 60

segments.oily: Reviewers with oily skin frequently describe the product as non-greasy with a matte to natural finish, though a couple mention some greasiness in the T-zone before it dries down.
segments.dry: A few reviewers with drier skin report pilling or a slightly drying feel, especially when layered with moisturizer or used without one.
segments.combination: Reviewers with combination skin report a natural, non-glowy finish that layers well under makeup.
segments.sensitive: Reviewers with sensitive or rosacea-prone skin describe it as non-irritating, fragrance-light, and gentle on the eyes and skin, with only occasional eye-stinging noted.
segments.mature: One reviewer using it for years alongside anti-aging goals credits it with helping maintain a youthful appearance, with no negative effects reported.

concerns.aging: One long-term user credits daily use with helping preserve a youthful look; no other aging-specific effects are reported.
concerns.dehydration: Several reviewers find it very lightweight and non-drying, but others note it can feel drying or cause pilling on dry patches, and one wished it were more moisturizing.
concerns.redness: One reviewer with rosacea reports it does not aggravate her skin, and another notes a reduction in redness over time; no reviewer reports increased redness.
concerns.barrier: No reviewer directly discusses barrier repair; sensitive-skin users report no irritation, suggesting it is well tolerated.
concerns.spots: One reviewer reports a reduction in dark spots and blemishes over time; this is not echoed elsewhere.
concerns.blemishes: Most acne-prone reviewers report no new breakouts and that it does not aggravate existing acne, though one reviewer describes general clogging concerns tied to pilling rather than breakouts.
concerns.oiliness: Most reviewers with oily skin describe a matte or natural finish with no added shine, though two mention initial greasiness that fades as it absorbs.

aspects.libelle: White cast on deeper skin tones
Pilling with certain moisturizers or makeup
Stings or burns eyes during sweating
Runny, watery consistency requiring careful application

extraits.texte: This was good for my oily skin however it did leave a white cast. My skin tone is medium deep and after a few minites of really rubbing the product in, it still left a white cast. Additionally, it did make my eyes burn and water.

This is probably the only sunscreen that doesnt break me out and works effectively. I was under the sun for about 3 hours straight and didn't completely obliterated by it, thanks to la roche posay! I really wanna test out the spray version to see if it works well over my makeup. The only downside is that I did get some pilling after applying it on top of my moisturizer. I had to dust off the residue with a face towel and reapply spf to the affected areas. It's pretty easy to work with, but might be an issue if youre in a rush.

Ive repurchased this product three time and added my 4th bottle to my cart. I have oily to combination skin, acne prone, and sensitive. This leaves my skin with a nice glow but not greasy. It can be used under make up as well, which is a plus. I have no regrets. Only down side is the cap, after a while sunscreen gets there and pile up. I have also tried the 100 on for Texas heat and works just as great!

extraits.titre: Holy grail spf for sensitive acne prone skin!
extraits.texte: I'm very picky when it comes to sunscreen since I have sensitive acne prone skin. A lot of them break me out and make me oily. They can be thick and hard to pair with other products or have a strong scent. This spf however doesn't have any of those issues! It truly marks all the boxes for me. It's super thin and liquidy. It pretty much blends itself. And leaves a dry to touch natural finish with no greasiness whatsoever. It doesn't irritate my eyes and looks great under makeup. You just have to make sure you shake it really, really well before application. It does seem a bit pricey but compared to other "drugstore" sunscreens you really get what you pay for. I consider this a drugstore luxury sunscreen lol it's also easy to reapply over makeup if needed.

I love love love this sunscreen! Blends into the skin nicely, no white tint, doesn't get too glowy or oily throughout the day (I have combination skin), and looks really nice under makeup. My skin sometimes gets sensitive too because of rosacea and this doesn't bother it.

The best sunscreen at the market, it is so good for my aging, rosacea, oily and very sensitive skin , the ingredients on it are very good for my skin instead of zinc oxide and titanium dioxide that burn my skin

This has been my tried and true since 2019, and I believe it's what helped me keep my youthful appearance. I am now 30 but still get mistaken for much younger, also want to mention I have oily skin and tend to break out easily but this sunscreen has never given me issues. I will say it does sting the eyes if you're out and sweating so watch out for that. I don't wear makeup but it works well with concealer and blush underneath. A few times I noticed it will appear patchy if you don't moisturize the night before or beforehand, but it's been no issue since I moisturize routinely. Very grateful my friend introduced this to me years ago
